title: Closest Divisors
summary: Determine two integers whose product is either num + 1 or num + 2, and have the smallest absolute difference.
statement: Determine two integers whose product is either num + 1 or num + 2, and have the smallest absolute difference. Return these integers in any order.
constraints: Choose two positive integers whose product is num+1 or num+2.
Minimize their absolute difference; return the pair in either order.
num is between one and one billion.
reference_solution:
def closest_factor_pair(num):
    best=None
    for value in (num+1,num+2):
        factor=int(value**0.5)
        while value%factor:factor-=1
        pair=[factor,value//factor]
        if best is None or pair[1]-pair[0]<best[1]-best[0]:best=pair
    return best

hints: The closest factor pair straddles the square root of its product.
For each of num+1 and num+2, search downward from its integer square root for the first divisor.
Compare the differences of the two resulting pairs and return the smaller.
The first divisor found below the square root maximizes the smaller factor and therefore minimizes the pair gap.
editorial: Search downward from floor(sqrt(value)) until a divisor is found for each candidate product. These are their respective closest factor pairs, so compare the two gaps. The oracle independently enumerates every divisor of both candidate values on seeded inputs.
